intelligence.human_view: Imagine a master workshop with shelves of perfect parts — gauges, jewels, boards — each made once, made right. The rule of the shop: you never whittle a copy of a part when the real one is on the shelf; you take it down and fit it. If something breaks, you don't tape it — you rebuild the joint so it can't break that way again. The price list isn't guessed; it's the owner's own numbers. And nothing leaves the shop until the owner's eye has passed it.
intelligence.simple_view: All the buttons in this place match, like a set of shiny buttons on one coat — we don't sew on a different button every day. There's ONE play button that reads the whole story out loud. The calendar is magic: tap a day and you see everything that happened that day. And here's the rule: just because the machine says 'done' doesn't mean it looks right — a person has to LOOK at it, with real eyes, before we say it's finished.
intelligence.grandma_view: Honesty in the small things is the whole reputation, dear. The baker who says 'the rolls are fresh but the pie needs an hour' gets your custom for life. The one who boxes a raw pie with a smile gets it once. Write it down, say it plain, finish what you start — and do it all for love of the people at your table.
